name: Kenaz
overview: Kenaz was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the father of Othniel and the brother of Caleb. His role is briefly noted in Scripture, highlighting his familial connections within the tribe. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Kenaz means 'hunting,' reflecting a proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning may suggest qualities associated with skill or pursuit, but Scripture does not elaborate further on this significance.
familyAndRelationships: Kenaz is explicitly identified as the brother of Caleb and is inferred to be the father of Othniel. Additionally, there is an implicit reference suggesting he was the father of Seraiah. These relationships place him within a notable family line in the tribe of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Kenaz holds significance in the biblical narrative primarily through his familial connections. As the father of Othniel, who is a notable figure, and brother to Caleb, Kenaz is part of a lineage that contributed to the leadership and inheritance within Judah. His mention underscores the importance of family heritage and tribal identity in God's providential plan.
